# ToggleButtonGroup accessibility conformance

Rated against WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA. See the [reports legend](../accessibility.md).

<!-- intro:start -->

ToggleButtonGroup coordinates a set of [Toggle Button](../ToggleButton/accessibility.md) children, so this report rates only the criteria that exist or change because of the grouping. Each toggle's own conformance (contrast, target size, label in name, focus indicator, keyboard activation, and the rest) is rated in the [Toggle Button report](../ToggleButton/accessibility.md) and listed under [Inherited from Toggle Button](#inherited-from-toggle-button).

Unlike a radio group, ToggleButtonGroup adds no roving tab order and no arrow-key navigation: it wraps the toggles in a `role="group"` container, and each toggle stays an independent tab stop that activates on its own. Keyboard operation and focus order are therefore inherited per toggle, not rated here.

<!-- intro:end -->

## Success criteria

### 🔍 Manual

#### 2.4.6 Headings and Labels · AA

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 2.4.6:start -->

- The group's label comes from the author's `aria-label`, the documented pattern ("text alignment" and "text formatting" in the demos).
- Whether the wording describes the set of choices depends on author content, a vague group label ("Options") would fail.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Read each toggle group's `aria-label`.
2. Confirm it describes the set of choices ("text alignment", not "Options").

<!-- 2.4.6:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 2.4.6:pass:start -->every group label describes the set of toggles it contains.<!-- 2.4.6:pass:end -->

### 🔁 Hybrid

#### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `ToggleButtonGroup.test.js`

<!-- 1.3.1:start -->

- ToggleButtonGroup sets `role="group"` on its root (`ToggleButtonGroup.js`), so the toggles are exposed as one related set. axe-core's `aria-roles` and `aria-allowed-attr` pass across the group demos.
- The group's accessible name is the author's to set with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; without one the grouping is exposed but unnamed.
- Confirmed by a unit test in [`./ToggleButtonGroup.test.js`](./ToggleButtonGroup.test.js).

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a screen reader running, move focus into the group and confirm the group and its name are announced (for example, "text alignment, group").
2. Render a group with no `aria-label` and confirm the group is exposed but unnamed.

<!-- 1.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.1:pass:start -->the toggles are exposed as one group, named when the author supplies a label.<!-- 1.3.1:pass:end -->

#### 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `ToggleButtonGroup.test.js` · axe-core `aria-allowed-attr` ✅, `aria-command-name` ✅, `aria-conditional-attr` ✅, `aria-deprecated-role` ✅, `aria-hidden-focus` ✅, `aria-prohibited-attr` ✅, `aria-required-attr` ✅, `aria-roles` ✅, `aria-valid-attr` ✅, `aria-valid-attr-value` ✅, `button-name` ✅, `nested-interactive` ✅

<!-- 4.1.2:start -->

- The group's role and value are met: `role="group"` names the relationship, and the selected value is exposed by each child's `aria-pressed`, which the group drives from its `value` and `exclusive` props (`ToggleButtonGroup.js`). axe-core `aria-roles`, `button-name`, and `nested-interactive` pass across the group demos.
- The group's name is the shared part, supplied by the author's `aria-label`.
- Confirmed by a unit test in [`./ToggleButtonGroup.test.js`](./ToggleButtonGroup.test.js).

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a screen reader running, focus each toggle in a group and confirm the group role, its author-supplied name, and each toggle's pressed state are announced.
2. Activate a toggle and confirm the pressed change is announced.

<!-- 4.1.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 4.1.2:pass:start -->the group exposes its role and author-supplied name, and each toggle's pressed state and its changes are announced.<!-- 4.1.2:pass:end -->

### ⚙️ Automated

#### 1.4.10 Reflow · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.10:start -->

- Each toggle sizes to its content, but the group owns the layout: a horizontal group is `display: inline-flex` and does not wrap (`ToggleButtonGroup.js`), so a wide row of toggles can overflow horizontally at 320 CSS pixels.
- The component provides `orientation="vertical"` as the escape hatch; the author keeps the group within 320 pixels by switching orientation or limiting the number of toggles. Covered by a Playwright test at a 320px viewport.

<!-- 1.4.10:end -->

## Not applicable

- **1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (AA), 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) (AA).** No audio or video.
- **1.3.4 Orientation (AA).** Sets no orientation lock; a layout concern.
- **1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA).** <!-- 1.3.5:start -->Not an input; collects no user data through `autocomplete`.<!-- 1.3.5:end -->
- **1.4.2 Audio Control (A).** Emits no audio.
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA).** <!-- 1.4.13:start -->The group shows no additional content on hover or focus; a `Tooltip` wrapper would own this.<!-- 1.4.13:end -->
- **2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (A).** <!-- 2.1.4:start -->The only keys are <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Space</kbd>, which are not single-character shortcuts.<!-- 2.1.4:end -->
- **2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (A).** Sets no time limit.
- **2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A).** <!-- 2.2.2:start -->Nothing moves or auto-updates.<!-- 2.2.2:end -->
- **2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (A).** Nothing flashes.
- **2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (A), 2.4.2 Page Titled (A), 2.4.5 Multiple Ways (AA).** Page or site structure, not a single component.
- **2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) (A).** <!-- 2.4.4:start -->The group renders no links.<!-- 2.4.4:end -->
- **2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (A), 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (A).** <!-- 2.5.1,2.5.4:start -->Toggles activate on a simple click; the group reads no device motion.<!-- 2.5.1,2.5.4:end -->
- **2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA).** <!-- 2.5.7:start -->Toggles select on tap or click; no drag operation.<!-- 2.5.7:end -->
- **3.1.1 Language of Page (A), 3.1.2 Language of Parts (AA).** <!-- 3.1.1,3.1.2:start -->The group emits no `<html lang>` and no text of its own.<!-- 3.1.1,3.1.2:end -->
- **3.2.3 Consistent Navigation (AA).** Covers repeated navigation across a set of pages, not a single component.
- **3.2.6 Consistent Help (A).** Covers consistent placement of help across pages.
- **3.3.1 Error Identification (A), 3.3.3 Error Suggestion (AA), 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) (AA).** <!-- 3.3.1,3.3.3,3.3.4:start -->The group collects and validates no input; these belong to the form or process.<!-- 3.3.1,3.3.3,3.3.4:end -->
- **3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (A).** <!-- 3.3.2:start -->Limited by WCAG to data-entry controls, and it excludes interactive components not associated with data entry. The group's children are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`, `role="button"`), not form fields, so the group is outside this criterion. (This is where ToggleButtonGroup differs from a radio group, whose native radios are data entry.)<!-- 3.3.2:end -->
- **3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A).** <!-- 3.3.7:start -->Covers repopulating previously entered data. The group captures none.<!-- 3.3.7:end -->
- **3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (AA).** <!-- 3.3.8:start -->The paste, autofill, and cognitive-test duty falls on the credential fields, not a toggle group.<!-- 3.3.8:end -->
- **4.1.3 Status Messages (AA).** <!-- 4.1.3:start -->The group emits no status messages; the selected value is exposed through each toggle's `aria-pressed`.<!-- 4.1.3:end -->

## Level AAA

<!-- level-aaa:start -->

The following SC are applicable but out of scope, and are item-level:

- **2.3.3 Animation from Interactions.** Each toggle's ripple `scale()` animation honors `prefers-reduced-motion` when the theme sets `motion.reducedMotion` to `system` or `always`; `disableRipple` also removes it. The default is `never`. `🚩`
- **2.4.13 Focus Appearance.** Each toggle's focus ripple is unlikely to meet the area and 3:1 thresholds, and `disableRipple` removes it. `🚩`
- **2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), 44 px.** Each toggle's `small` size (about 40 px) is below 44 px. `🚩`
- **1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced), 7:1.** Palettes target the AA 4.5:1, so several selected toggle colors fall short of 7:1. `🚩`
- Also touched, in the same shape as their A and AA siblings: **1.3.6 Identify Purpose, 1.4.9 Images of Text (No Exception), 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception), 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)**.

<!-- level-aaa:end -->

## Scope and test environment

- **Standard.** WCAG 2.2, Level A and AA.
- **Component version.** `@mui/material` 9.4.0.

- **Scope.** The ToggleButtonGroup component coordinating two or more `ToggleButton` children, with an author-supplied `aria-label` for the group's name, rendered through the documented API.
